items.headline: 270,000 Square Miles Around Easter Island to Become Indigenous-Managed Ocean Reserve
items.facts: Indigenous residents of Easter Island will hold a voting majority on a sea council governing a new 270,000‑square‑mile marine reserve, outnumbering Chilean officials 6 to 5.

framing.publicBrief: It is 2 a.m. in the council chamber. The vote on the new 270,000-square-mile marine reserve is final. Rapa Nui indigenous residents hold six seats. Chile holds five. The majority decides who manages the waters. The gavel is ready.

roleFlavor.contributor: You hold one vote in a tight majority. Your side controls the outcome.

howItWorks: The council votes on management rights.
Rapa Nui residents hold six seats.
Chile holds five seats.
The majority vote decides the fate of the reserve.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: How do you cast your vote?

items.headline: Temporary Dumpster Rentals for Permit-Restricted Zones and Right-of-Way Areas
items.facts: Contractors renting temporary dumpsters in permit‑restricted zones must plan and document usage to avoid fines or work stoppages.

framing.narrativeTitle: Dumpster Deal in a Permit‑Restricted Zone
framing.publicBrief: At two a.m., contractors have hired temporary dumpsters in a zone that requires a special permit. Municipal authorities have warned that any unapproved use will lead to fines or a work stoppage. The contractors must decide whether to keep the dumpsters and risk penalties or return them and halt their project.

roleFlavor.proposer: Contractors who need the dumpsters to keep the job moving
roleFlavor.responder: Municipal authorities who enforce the permit rules

howItWorks: The contractors can keep the dumpsters and face potential fines or work stoppage.
The authorities can enforce the permit and stop the dumpsters from operating.
Both sides see the same facts about the zone and the contract.

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Both sides agree to a permit; the contractors keep the dumpsters and pay a fee.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: Contractors ignore the rule and keep the dumpsters; authorities fine them and halt work.
outcomes.MIXED: Contractors keep the dumpsters but authorities issue a warning, allowing work to continue with caution.

items.headline: How Florida quietly removed climate change content from textbooks
items.facts: Florida requested publishers to dilute climate change content, and publishers complied.

framing.publicBrief: The sun sets over the state capital. Florida state has asked publishers to remove climate change facts from new school books. The publishers must decide what to do. They can keep the science in, or they can edit it out to please the state. If they refuse, they lose the right to sell books in Florida. If they agree, the books are approved. The publishers want to sell books. The state wants its books to match its rules. The deadline is now.

roleFlavor.proposer: You are Florida state. You set the rules for what goes into school books. You decide if a book is good enough for students.
roleFlavor.responder: You are the publishers. You write and print the books. You need the state's approval to sell them in schools.

howItWorks: Florida state sets the rules for the books.
Publishers must choose to follow or ignore them.
If publishers ignore the rules, they lose sales.
If they follow, the books are approved.

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Publishers remove climate content. Books are approved.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: Publishers keep climate content. Books are rejected.
outcomes.MIXED: Publishers argue. The deal is uncertain.

items.headline: US Appeals Court Overturns Trump’s Order To Break Up Delta Air Lines & Aeromexico Joint Venture
items.facts: The US Court of Appeals overturned a Trump administration order blocking Delta and Aeromexico’s joint venture, allowing the airlines to continue their partnership.

framing.narrativeTitle: Delta and Aeromexico Keep Their Joint Venture
framing.publicBrief: The US Court of Appeals has ruled that the Trump administration order blocking the joint venture between Delta Air Lines and Aeromexico is invalid. The airlines can now keep their partnership. The US Department of Transportation had tried to stop the partnership, but the court said the order was unlawful. The airlines and the department now must decide how to move forward. The partnership is a major business deal for both airlines. The court’s decision changes the rules of the game. The airlines can keep the joint venture and the department can try to enforce new rules.

roleFlavor.proposer: Delta Air Lines and Aeromexico are the airlines who want to keep their joint venture
roleFlavor.responder: The US Department of Transportation is the agency that tried to stop the joint venture

howItWorks: Delta and Aeromexico want to keep their partnership
The department wants to enforce antitrust rules
Both sides must decide whether to comply with the court or fight it
The decision will affect future airline deals
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Decide how to respond to the court’s ruling

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Both sides accept the court’s decision and the partnership continues
outcomes.BETRAYAL: The department rejects the ruling and tries to enforce new rules
outcomes.MIXED: One side accepts while the other disputes the ruling

items.headline: The Next Dollar: Three Competing Strategies at Lindblad, Intrepid, and Travelopia
items.facts: Lindblad, Intrepid Travel and Travelopia are each pursuing different investment strategies in the adventure travel market.

framing.publicBrief: Lindblad, Intrepid Travel, and Travelopia are chasing the same customers in adventure travel. Each firm has picked a different way to win. Lindblad leans on its deep history. Intrepid Travel pushes small groups. Travelopia bets on low prices. They can all survive if they stay in their lanes. If two firms try to own the same niche, they will bleed cash fighting each other. The market is big enough for three, but only if they do not step on each other’s toes.

roleFlavor.hunter: You run one of these three brands. You see the maps and the margins. You know that sharing the market keeps profits high. You also see the temptation to grab the other guy’s customers, even if it star

STAG.label: Hold Your Lane
STAG.meaning: You stick to your current strategy and ignore the other firm’s customers.
STAG.outcome: Both firms keep their profits. The market stays stable and everyone makes money.

HARE.label: Grab Their Share
HARE.meaning: You try to steal customers from the other firm by undercutting them.
HARE.outcome: You gain some customers, but the other firm fights back. Profits drop for both of you.

howItWorks: You and the other firm choose at the same time.
You cannot see what the other firm picks until after you commit.
If you both hold your lanes, you both win big.
If you both try to grab share, you both lose money.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Do you play safe or fight for share?

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Both firms stay in their lanes. Profits remain high for everyone.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: One firm grabbed share. The other held back. The grabber won a little.
outcomes.MIXED: Both firms tried to grab share. A price war started. Profits fell for both.

items.headline: OpenAI is gaining on Anthropic with business users, new data indicates
items.facts: Ramp data shows Anthropic holding about 44% market share of U.S. business users while OpenAI holds about 40%.

framing.publicBrief: Ramp data shows a tight race for U.S. business users. Anthropic holds 44% share. OpenAI holds 40%. Both companies want to grow their user base. They must decide how to reach these businesses. OpenAI is gaining ground on Anthropic.

roleFlavor.hunter: You lead a tech giant. You need to keep or grow your slice of the market. Your rivals are watching your every move.

STAG.label: Target Big Deals
STAG.meaning: Focus on winning large, complex contracts.
STAG.outcome: You aim for the biggest share of the market.

HARE.label: Take Safe Share
HARE.outcome: You secure a steady but smaller portion.

howItWorks: Both companies choose their sales strategy at the same time.
Neither side can see the other's plan before acting.
If both aim for the same big deals, they split the gain.
If one aims big and one aims small, they avoid conflict.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: How do you grow your user base?

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Both sides target different customer needs.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: One side steals the other's target deals.
outcomes.MIXED: Strategies clash or overlap in the market.
